facets.description: utilities.js:182 – the flat 10MB client check ignores max_attachment_size_kb, so for attachments the client rejects files the server would accept, or accepts files the server will reject.
Images that still exceed max_image_size_kb after the server's 5 downsize passes get past the 10MB client check and are then rejected by the server.
utilities.js:183-184 – the file_too_large alert in the validator shows 10240 KB as the maximum instead of the configured limit.
utilities.js:243-249 – the 413 handler also shows 10240 KB as the maximum regardless of the configured limit. This needs its own edit at line 246.

answer.reasoning:
The 413 handler sets maxSizeKB again at line 246, so it needs its own edit. I treat it as a separate facet (F4). The validator alert (F3) is fixed by the same line-182 change as F1.

- **s_ee27a71c:** reports the attachment mismatch in both directions (F1). It also reports the wrong maximum in both the alert and the 413 handler (F3, F4). It names max_image_size_kb only as context, so it doesn't cover images that can't be shrunk enough (F2).
- **s_99672758:** reports only the attachment problem (F1).
- **s_7b3553a9:** reports attachments (F1) and images that can't be shrunk enough (F2). It hints at the message mismatch: the server's error text won't match the 10MB the client advertised. I count that, loosely, as F3. It never mentions the 413 handler (F4).

So no member is complete. This is not decisive because two calls are judgment calls: splitting the 413 handler into its own facet, and counting s_7b3553a9's indirect message remark as F3. If the error message were one combined facet, s_7b3553a9 could count as complete, as Labeler 1 found.
